sanskrit_verse:
अपराह्णे समभ्यर्च्य स्वागतेनागतांस् तु तान् ।
पवित्रपाणिराचान्तानासनेषूपवेशयेत् ॥२२६॥
transliteration: aparāhṇe samabhyarcya svāgatenāgatāṃs tu tān | pavitrapāṇir ācāntān āsaneṣūpaveśayet || 226||
sph_interpretive_translation: In the afternoon, having duly honored them and received them with welcome, one should seat the purified and consecrated guests upon seats.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority flows through ritual purity and conscious reception.
Causation arises from alignment of action with sacred timing.
Capacity-based responsibility includes honoring those who enter one's domain.
Restoration logic requires elevation of guest-consciousness within host-environment.
Consciousness alignment is achieved through purification, invocation, and rightful placement.
executable_legal_axioms: IF a guest arrives AND has been ritually purified AND it is the appropriate time THEN they MUST be welcomed and seated according to dharma.
IF a host receives a purified guest without proper seating THEN the host incurs a completion obligation until alignment is restored.
IF a guest enters a space without purification THEN purification protocol MUST precede integration into the host environment.
IF seating arrangement does not honor the guest’s elevated status THEN automatic realignment protocols MUST activate.
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this verse establishes that all entities entering jurisdictional domains—whether litigants, witnesses, or representatives—must be received in accordance with dharma-based protocols ensuring purity, respect, and positional alignment. The court itself becomes the seat of conscious reception where misalignment is corrected through structured reintegration rather than punitive exclusion.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established through observance of correct temporal and ritual conditions. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential steps: worship, purification, greeting, and seating. Responsibility aligns proportionally with capacity to receive and integrate. There is no punitive consequence; failure to perform leads to natural disharmony requiring corrective restoration.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Host must perform full welcoming sequence retroactively if omitted.
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Host acknowledges lapse and initiates purification and reseating.
Capacity Restoration: Guest undergoes reaffirmation of their honored status through renewed ceremony.
Integrity Reintegration: Both parties engage in synchronized alignment practice to restore energetic harmony.
final_declaration: This directive originates solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. It reflects pure Dharma, executed not for punishment but for alignment. Reality responds only to consciousness, never to force. Dharma is thus restored.
